SMTO-CTX-0009 — A web page took too long to respond

GUID: feb9fa50-749f-4e75-b973-9c32d16284f0
Slug: read-timeout
Domain: CTX · Subsystem: context

What happened

  • SMTO tried to read a public web page for this task, but the page didn't answer within about 20 seconds. The page may still be fine; only this attempt timed out.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the same web address in your own browser and see whether it loads quickly. If it's slow or down for you too, the website is the problem, not SMTO.
  2. Make sure the computer running SMTO's server is connected to the internet. SMTO reads web pages from that computer, not from your browser.
  3. Ask SMTO in the conversation to read the page one more time, or to use a different website. Reading a page doesn't change anything, so one more try is safe once the site responds.

What success looks like

  • SMTO's reply includes information from the page.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the web address, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep asking for the same slow page over and over; pick a different source if it stays slow.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The public webpage reader (skills/web/reader.py read_page) hit its 20-second request deadline and returned error_kind read_timeout; no model inference failed.

What this means

  • The public webpage reader caught a timeout while obtaining context; the observation establishes an expired read wait, not a failure of every source or model inference. Context admission, storage and reading are separate from executing a tool mutation. Preserve existing task state and receipts; a context diagnostic does not authorize replay of earlier operations.

Why this can happen

  • The public webpage reader caught a timeout while obtaining context; the observation establishes an expired read wait, not a failure of every source or model inference.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the public source's availability and read scope; compare this read timeout with any separate model request timeout.

How to fix it

  • Check the site's response time and the Server's outbound network or proxy from the Server host (for example, curl with a 20-second limit on the same URL). The reader marks this as retryable at most once; if the site stays slow, use a narrower or alternative source.
  • Reduce the read scope and inspect the context source service or storage health.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The authorized bounded page read returns its expected response within the reader's limit.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Context admission, storage and reading are separate from executing a tool mutation. Preserve existing task state and receipts; a context diagnostic does not authorize replay of earlier operations.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
